rules.statement: When a shared helper method takes a long list of positional parameters, especially several of the same type such as strings, and the same group of inputs recurs across sibling methods, group those inputs into a small sealed descriptor type that is built once and passed instead, so that each method takes at most one or two other inputs besides its context and the cancellation token.
rules.why: Long positional argument lists make call sites hard to read, and swapping two same-typed arguments such as a name and a path still compiles, so the mistake only shows up at runtime.
rules.check: Look for new or changed methods with roughly six or more parameters before the CancellationToken, particularly with two or more string (or other same-typed) parameters, where the same subset of parameters is repeated across several related methods; ask for a sealed descriptor/record that bundles them.
